To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. We develop a new framework to understand the role of prior in VAEs, 2. The β-VAE can be seen as a special case of the new framework, 3. We show that a simple modification of the prior allows to obtain disentangled representations with little to no loss in reconstruction quality

(i) the decomposition framework is a useful tool for understanding and improving VAEs, (ii) the β-VAEs can be improved by simple changes to the prior, and (iii) the β-regularization is invariant to rotations and therefore cannot be used to control the structure of the representation.

1) disentanglement is not a single objective but a decomposition of the representation space into a number of independent components, 2) the standard choice of a Gaussian prior for the β-VAEs is invariant to rotations, and 3) this invariance can be removed to yield better disentangling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a generalisation of the disentanglement problem in VAEs that permits a wider class of objectives and priors to be used, which can yield a more flexible range of latent representations.
understanding the disentanglement properties of VAEs and developing a generalised framework that allows for more flexible and effective learning of disentangled representations.
understanding the disentangling properties of the β-VAEs and their generalisation, and developing methods to better control the decomposition in the learnt representation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the β- and α-VAE are not disentangling VAEs.
the β-FAE (factor analysis VAE) is the most flexible and powerful VAE variant for learning disentangled representations.
the decomposition of the latent representation is a generalisation of the notion of disentanglements and the β-VAEs can be seen as a special case.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

disentanglement is not a single objective, but a spectrum of properties that can be imposed on the latent space, and that VAEs can be used to learn a wide variety of representations, depending on the choice of the prior.
we have developed a generalisation of VAE disentanglement and demonstrated how the standard VAE can be modified in order to achieve better disentanglements.
we propose a generalisation of the notion of disentanglements in VAEs and show that the current standard for disentangled VAEs, the β-VAEs, can be improved by a simple manipulation of the prior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the notion of disentanglements is much richer and more flexible than previously thought.
decomposition is a more general concept than disentanglement and that the latter can be obtained as a special case of the former.
disentanglement is an emergent property of the VAE and that it should not be considered in isolation from the prior, but instead be viewed as a decomposition of the representation.
